title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is a fraud carried out with a synthetic likeness, not a model making an error on its own. The deepfake video and voice were used to impersonate a public figure on a live WhatsApp call, and the impersonation was the entry point for a sequence of payment demands from people who claimed to be a manager and a CBI officer. The AI-generated media did not act alone; it was the opening move in a social-engineering script executed by people on the other end of the call.

The failure sits at the point of contact between a synthetic identity and a target who had no way to verify it. Nothing in the reporting indicates that the platform or the payment app performed any check on whether the person on the call was who he appeared to be. Catching this would have required verification of the caller's identity through a channel independent of the call itself, or a check at the payment stage on where the money was going. Neither is described as having happened.

What is not established is who produced the deepfake, whether the same operation has targeted others, or whether any suspect has been identified; a police case has been registered, and a case is not a finding of guilt.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using a deepfake video and voice to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said a manager would arrange the transfer. The manager then demanded fees, including Rs 5,000 as exchange charges and Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN.

Another person claiming to be a CBI officer demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine. Giri paid more than Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app before refusing a further Rs 50,000 demand and realizing he had been cheated. He contacted the cybercrime helpline and then Byappanahalli police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. This is the city's first reported deepfake case of its kind.
